Saniye hoca is one of the best instructors that you can take philosophy courses in Bilkent. She is always student friendly. It is great that she gives us a chance to get feedback before almost every assignment. She makes sure that we comprehend the subject and she is open to answer any questions we have without patronizing the student. She is very respectful and even curious about our thoughts and arguments, which is very important in a Phil course, I think. course: The strongest aspect is that the course makes us learn/strengthen our skills of critical thinking. It is also important for the students of social sciences to learn how the major philosophers approach some of the matters such as justice and ethics, and how such concepts developed over time. However, as the weak aspect, the course is really challenging. It is essential to learn what the instructors expect. There is too much workload and the texts are hard to read. Almost all of them require for us to read an explanation from websites even though the instructors explain them clearly and in full detail.

instructor:
It was very nice taking this course from this instructor because she really knows the topic to the fullest. It's been illuminating to see a woman philosopher who has such a good grasp on her own topic. 
One suggestion I have is that maybe the course objectives could have been delivered better. She was friendly with giving us extra time on our assignments, but even so, her coursework demands changed too much throughout the course. Other than that, she is amazing.

Saniye Hoca is simply excellent. She is helpful, empathetic, and a fair grader. She has a full grasp of and respect for the material she teaches. She knows that Kant is hard to understand; at the beginning of the semester, she provided us with enough scaffolding to understand Kant’s general philosophy and arguments in the first two critiques. In class, she is extremely kind; for instance, when you say something wrong about Kant, she explains his view over and over again patiently, with understanding, and with utmost genuine concern for her profession. At the beginning of the semester, I sometimes thought I should not have taken this course because Kant is notoriously difficult to read, and the first part of the third critique does not necessarily make much sense in the beginning. But, after taking her course, I’m convinced that the third critique is a necessary part of Kant’s corpus, as opposed to the views of some other scholars in the literature. Often, I left the classroom thinking that it was fortunate for me to have taken Kant from a scholar such as Dr. Vatansever, who genuinely cares for the value we can get from Kant and the history of philosophy. It would have been better if we had studied the first critique; this is no doubt. But she covered the necessary and crucial parts of the first critique and made enough dents into its arguments. Most importantly, I noticed that my understanding of the primary text improved 100% after listening to her lectures and after going over the notes I took during the lecture. It would have been completely unbearable to read Kant on our own without her lecturing.

It was a pleasure and honor to get a course from Professor Vatansever. As a female Turkish philosopher, I admire her work and teaching style. She is amazing in giving lectures, guiding in our in-class discussions, and giving feedbacks on our outlines, essay drafts, and presentations. She is approachable, understanding, and sympathetic to our responsibilities, obligations and commitments. She was so helpful in every aspect of the course.
course: A weakest aspect of the course was that there were a number of uncertainties about the logistics of the course. For instance, the deadlines for the papers, the dates of the presentations, and so on kept changing. Such vagueness afflicted a bit.

This is a very hard course. Saniye could have been more organized and managed her time better by assigning the relevant readings for the week. Instead, it was disorganized. But she explain the topic very well so it was nice. Also, she change the requirements A LOT and that was confusing to me. Maybe she could be more open?

The secondary texts were selected carefully and made it easier to understand the primary text. However, the design of the course and the syllabus might benefit from a re-evaluation. For instance, reading the first critique might have made more sense. Or, it might have made more sense to spend more time on the second part (teleological judgments) of the third critique and less time on the first part (aesthetic judgments). Finally, maybe presentations are not that crucial for this course; I would have preferred to listen to lectures instead, but I realize that this is a completely personal and nerdy attitude.
